title: Hydatidiform Mole: Complete vs Partial Mole & Post-Molar hCG Surveillance
subject: ss-gynaecological-oncology
refs: FIGO Cancer Report 2021: Gestational Trophoblastic Disease

steps.say: Complete hydatidiform moles result from the fertilization of an enucleated ovum by paternal chromosomes. The resulting diploid conceptus possesses purely androgenetic genetic material.
steps.tx: A **complete mole** is genetically **diploid androgenetic** containing **no maternal DNA**, resulting from the fertilization of an **empty ovum** by a haploid sperm that duplicates (**46,XX (90%)** in **90** percent) or by two sperms (**46**,XY in **10** percent), characterized by diffuse hydropic villi, circumferential trophoblastic hyperplasia, and absent embryonic tissue.

vis.caption: FIGO anatomical staging and FIGO-WHO score matrix for GTN. Credit: StewardMD.
vis.alt: Gestational trophoblastic disease staging and scoring

steps.say: Partial hydatidiform moles arise through dispermic fertilization of a normal maternal oocyte. The conceptus is triploid with two paternal sets and one maternal chromosome complement.
steps.tx: A **partial mole** is genetically **triploid diandric** (**69,XXY** in **70** percent, 69,XXX, or 69,XYY), arising from the fertilization of an intact haploid ovum (containing **23** maternal chromosomes) by two paternal sperms (**two paternal sets**). It is distinguished by scalloped villi, focal trophoblastic atypia, and the **presence of fetal tissue**.

left.title: Complete Hydatidiform Mole
points: Complete absence of fetal or embryonic tissues
Diffuse hydropic villi with circumferential trophoblastic hyperplasia
Post-molar GTN malignant risk is 15% to 20%

right.title: Partial Hydatidiform Mole
points: Presence of fetal erythrocytes, amnion, or embryo
Focal hydropic swelling with scalloped villous outlines
Post-molar GTN malignant risk is low (1% to 5%)

steps.say: Immunohistochemical evaluation of p57 expression reliably distinguishes complete from partial moles. Because p57 is a maternally transcribed gene, complete moles exhibit absent nuclear staining.
steps.tx: **p57KIP2 IHC** (p**57** protein expression, encoded by the **paternally imprinted maternal gene** CDKN1C) is an indispensable diagnostic biomarker: because maternal alleles are absent, a **complete mole p57-negative** shows absent nuclear staining in cytotrophoblast and villous stroma, whereas a **partial mole p57-positive** shows strong nuclear positivity in **2** tissue layers.

steps.say: Surgical uterine evacuation should be performed promptly using suction curettage under real time ultrasound visualization. Medical oxytocic induction must be avoided to prevent pulmonary embolism.
steps.tx: Uterine evacuation requires **suction curettage 10-12 mm** (**10** to **12** mm vacuum cannula) under continuous **ultrasound guidance**. There is strict **avoidance of medical induction** (prostaglandins or high-dose oxytocin before evacuation) due to severe **trophoblastic embolization risk** to maternal pulmonary circulation.

nodes.label: Establish diagnosis of hydatidiform mole on pelvic ultrasound
Crossmatch blood and prepare for suction curettage in operating theater
Perform gentle suction curettage with 10-12 mm cannula under direct ultrasound
Start intravenous oxytocin infusion only after significant volume evacuation

steps.say: The biological risk of malignant post molar trophoblastic neoplasia varies sharply between complete and partial gestations. Complete moles carry a substantial risk of persistent disease.
steps.tx: The **post-molar GTN risk** after molar evacuation varies markedly by genetic subtype: a **complete mole 15-20%** (**15** to **20** percent) risk of malignant persistence (invasive mole or choriocarcinoma), whereas a **partial mole 1-5%** (**1** to **5** percent) risk of malignant progression, rarely ever metastasizing.

left.title: Complete Mole Persistence Factors
points: High-risk features: age >40, pre-evacuation hCG >100,000 mIU/mL
Theca lutein ovarian cysts >6 cm and excessive uterine enlargement

right.title: Partial Mole Persistence Factors
points: Extremely rare progression to metastatic choriocarcinoma
Shorter surveillance requirement once hCG normalizes

steps.say: Post evacuation monitoring relies on serial quantitative serum human chorionic gonadotropin measurements. Surveillance protocols dictate weekly testing until negative levels are documented.
steps.tx: Rigorous post-evacuation **hCG surveillance** requires **weekly until negative for 3 weeks** (serum beta-hCG <**5** mIU/mL across **3** consecutive weeks), followed by **monthly for 6 months** (**6** months) in complete moles, and **1** confirmation month in partial moles to document remission and detect early GTN.

nodes.label: Complete suction evacuation of hydatidiform mole
Obtain baseline serum quantitative beta-hCG within 48 hours
Monitor serum hCG weekly until levels are normal (<5 mIU/mL) for 3 weeks
Continue monthly hCG surveillance for 6 months post-normalization

steps.say: Reliable contraception is mandatory throughout the human chorionic gonadotropin surveillance interval to avoid confounding rising levels with pregnancy. Intrauterine devices are temporarily contraindicated.
steps.tx: Strict **contraception during hCG monitoring** (oral contraceptive pills, barrier methods, or depot medroxyprogesterone) is mandatory for 6 months to prevent pregnancy from obscuring GTN diagnosis. There is a **contraindication to IUD before normalization** due to risk of uterine perforation and hemorrhage into vascular trophoblastic tissue.

rows: Suppresses pituitary LH cross-reactivity and prevents pregnancy
High efficacy without increasing post-molar GTN risk
Risk of uterine perforation into subinvolution / vascular choriocarcinoma
Zero systemic effects, but higher real-world failure rate

steps.say: Recurrent hydatidiform moles are rare but may stem from maternal effect gene mutations. Biallelic alterations in NLRP7 or KHDC3L disrupt normal oocyte genomic imprinting.
steps.tx: While molar recurrence is rare (1-2%), **familial recurrent biparental mole** represents an autosomal recessive disorder caused by biallelic **NLRP7 mutation** (accounting for **75** percent of familial cases with gene on chromosome **7**) or **KHDC3L mutation** (chromosome **3**), causing maternal **imprinting failure** during oogenesis.
